text:
Matt Coronato is on pace for a career year, as The Hockey Writers pointed out this week, and the shape of it is a little unusual. He has 19 points in 27 games, eight on the power play, and four goals in his last ten, including one each in Ottawa and New Jersey this week.

What makes us hesitate is the five-on-five picture. Calgary gets just 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him bottom 1% of forwards defensively last season, with opponents piling up chances while he played. His own chances are down too, 0.73 expected goals per 60 against 0.99 last year, so his scoring rate is a touch above what our numbers think he can hold.

The case for him comes from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, which had him 98th percentile for chances from the slot and 93rd for setting up shots last season. That's a real offensive skill set. His minutes are climbing, up almost a minute and a half over his last ten. Our range has him at 48 to 67 points; the defense decides whether he keeps those minutes.
